title: Virtues of Spending in Allah's Way
summary: Spending in Allah's way has great virtues as per Quran and hadith.
translation: In the Holy Quran and blessed Hadiths, the virtue of spending in the way of Allah is immensely emphasized. The Quran encourages by stating that whatever a person does is in the knowledge of Allah, meaning that Allah will certainly reward and bless you for it. "Whatever good you do, Allah knows it," and in another place, "Whatever you spend of good is for yourself, and whatever you spend, seek only Allah's face, and whatever you spend will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged." Similarly, in a noble hadith narrated by Abdullah bin Masood (may Allah be pleased with him), it is said that there are two types of people who can be envied for the blessings Allah has given them. In Islam, envy is generally prohibited. Envy means wishing for the removal of someone else's blessing and hoping it is bestowed upon oneself. However, scholars interpret envy here as 'Ghibtah', which means desiring a similar blessing without wishing for its removal from the other person. Thus, 'no envy except in two cases': one, a man whom Allah has given wealth, which he uses in a rightful way, and two, a man whom Allah has endowed with wisdom which he uses for judgment and teaches to others. Therefore, one can legitimately aspire to these two qualities alone.
